# WO-604: Exposure check fetches a broker page it cannot read (needless disclosure)
Status: queued (in-house; Codex lane file, vendors offline)
Vendor: claude
Agent: automation-engineer (Theo Park)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: engine
Tier: deep
Severity: MEDIUM
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
`exposure --refresh` sent the owner's name and city in a search URL to the one `open` broker, got HTTP 403, and would have failed anyway: `_read()` checks `broker.search` only after the fetch (`engine/exposure.py:433-440`), and that broker has no `search:` spec. Every such request tells a data broker that someone is looking up this person, for no possible benefit (data minimization, shared rule 6 spirit). The same order applies to the old-address, previous-name and extra-value pages.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. If `broker.search` is None or has no `result_selector`, the broker is "check by hand" with reason `no_parser` and NO fetch happens (main page and every extra page).
2. Same guard in `check_one` before the polite gap, so no delay is spent either.
3. Test: fake broker with `search_access: open`, a pattern and no `search` spec; a fetcher that fails the test if called; result is check_by_hand/no_parser; the Event detail has ids/enums only.
4. Existing exposure tests unchanged and passing.

## Tasks
- [ ] 1. Move the parser check ahead of the fetch.
- [ ] 2. Test with a must-not-be-called fetcher.
